items.title: What is an agentic web resolver?
items.shortAnswer: An agentic web resolver discovers the machine- and agent-facing interfaces a website actually exposes, preserves where each observation came from, reports conflicts, and selects an interface for a concrete intent.

items.title: MCP vs A2A vs WebMCP vs llms.txt
items.shortAnswer: MCP, A2A, WebMCP and llms.txt solve different layers: backend tool/context exchange, agent-to-agent interaction, browser-page tool exposure, and text-oriented content routing respectively.

items.title: Agentic web resolver
items.definition: Software that discovers multiple machine- and agent-facing interfaces exposed by a website, preserves provenance, reports conflicts and selects an interface for a concrete intent.

items.title: Resolver regret
items.definition: A decision-quality case where a simpler discovery strategy selects the reviewed-correct interface while the union Resolver selects an incorrect one.

items.title: Discovery conflict
items.definition: A disagreement between independently observed or publisher-declared discovery sources that a resolver preserves rather than silently overwriting.

items.title: ARWP vs alternatives — agent readiness, interoperability and AI visibility tools
items.shortAnswer: ARWP is project-classified as an agentic web interoperability resolver. AgentReady/Ora is the closest adjacent readiness standard/scanner; WebMCP scanners, crawler-control products and AI visibility platforms solve narrower or complementary decisions.

items.title: ARWP vs AgentReady / Ora
items.shortAnswer: AgentReady/Ora defines and measures product readiness for agents; ARWP resolves the heterogeneous interfaces a website actually exposes, preserves provenance and conflicts, and selects an interface for a concrete intent without a universal readiness score.

items.title: ARWP vs Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)
items.shortAnswer: ARD is an upstream federated catalog and search specification for agentic resources. ARWP is a site-first interoperability resolver and should consume ARD as one discovery source alongside ordinary web, API, A2A, MCP, Skills and trust evidence.

items.title: Static metadata vs runtime evidence
items.shortAnswer: Static metadata can establish that a publisher advertises an interface; runtime evidence can establish that a protocol endpoint or browser capability responds as observed. Neither alone proves authorization, trustworthiness or task success.

items.title: State of the Agentic Web — Foundation Release
items.shortAnswer: Frozen foundation research release: 20 independent documentation sites, 100 reviewed intent decisions; llms-aware 89/100, resolver-union 86/100, resolver regret 6 and uniquely-correct union 0. The cohort is explicitly not representative of the public web.

items.title: ARWP Evidence Receipts
items.shortAnswer: Append-only integrity-verified ARWP Resolver observations. Receipt integrity proves the stored observation was not silently modified; it does not prove publisher endorsement, authorization or trustworthiness.

items.title: ARWP public reference observation — 2026-09-05
items.shortAnswer: Live owner-controlled reference observation captured by GitHub Actions: 3 of 10 discovery sources resolved, 34 interfaces normalized, 0 conflicts. This is interoperability evidence, not independent adoption evidence.

items.title: A2A 1.0 callable interfaces come from supportedInterfaces, not the Agent Card discovery URL
items.shortAnswer: For A2A 1.0, an Agent Card is discovery metadata; clients select a supported interface and use the URL declared by the selected supportedInterfaces[] entry.

items.title: Resolver union still trails llms-aware on the frozen reviewed 20-site corpus after the OpenAPI search eligibility correction
items.shortAnswer: Frozen 2026-08-28 result: llms-aware 89/100, resolver-union 86/100, resolver regret 6, resolver uniquely correct 0.
